event.details: Mudgala resumes Brahmā’s creation: Brahmins from mouth, Kṣatriyas arms, Vaiśyas thighs, Śūdras feet; renunciation from head, forest-stage heart, brahmacarya navel and household-state lower legs. Dharma chest and Adharma back set god/demon courses; gods/Gandharvas/Apsarases/Yakṣas/Asuras/Yātudhānas, snakes/birds/beasts/humans arise from his body. They act yet do not multiply. These are source-local cosmological body-emergences, not universal biological descent claims.

event.details: Mudgala classifies nine creations: first mahat, second tanmātra/bhūta, third vaikārika/indriya (three prākṛta); fourth stationary beings, fifth tiryak, sixth upward-flow gods, seventh downward-flow humans, eighth bhautika beings, ninth kaumāra (six vaikṛta). The first three are described as buddhi-pūrva, guiding creatures through principles. Brahmā is distressed that his diverse creatures do not multiply.

event.details: A couple emerges from Brahmā: Śatarūpā from left limb and Svāyambhuva Manu from right, first knowledgeable in Kṣatriya dharma. They ask orders; he directs sexual procreation through tapas. They bow, go to forest and practice intense Gaṇeśa meditation. Kardama emerges from Brahmā’s shadow, is ordered to create, then goes to forest desiring progeny and meditates on white-form Viṣṇu with prescribed tapas.

event.details: Svāyambhuva Manu with wife goes to forest, performs intense tapas by eight-syllable procedure1000 DIVINE years and gains Gaṇeśa’s appearance. He bows, worships and hymns elephant/Human-elephant/Oṃ form, four arms, mouse vehicle, Svānanda, Siddhi/Buddhi and yoga, saying vision inspires praise and blesses father/tapas/knowledge/lineage/learning/vows. Gaṇeśa raises him, offers a boon and promises his hymn readers/hearers all ends, progeny/prosperity, sorrow removal, wealth/grain, four aims/Brahman and firm devotion.

event.details: Manu requests firm Gaṇeśa devotion eliminating delusion, capacity to create, excellent dharma maintenance, lasting protection of subjects, success in every wish and continual dwelling among Gaṇeśa devotees. Gaṇeśa assents to Manu, vanishes and goes to his own realm.

event.details: Manu and Śatarūpā bow to Brahmā and depart at his order; Manu rules dharmically, armed and fond of Gaṇapatyas. Through sexual union they produce sons Priyavrata/Uttānapāda and daughters Ākūti/Devahūti/Prasūti. He gives Prasūti to Dakṣa, Ākūti to Ruci and Devahūti to Kardama. Kardama’s100-year Viṣṇu tapas gains appearance; he asks Viṣṇu as son, receives grant, and Viṣṇu as Kapila becomes his son in Devahūti. Ruci’s mānasa twin Yajña/Dakṣiṇā is born in Ākūti; Yajña Viṣṇu fathers12 Yāma gods in Dakṣiṇā. With wife/sages he makes a jeweled four-armed Gaṇeśa image, constantly worships by yoga; Gaṇeśa gives marvelous yoga. Yajña becomes foremost Gaṇapatya yogin, chants Heramba and teaches disciples Gaṇapatya yoga.
